question: Tuhin Kanta Pandey succeeded whom as the chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhabi Puri Buch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Madhabi Puri Buch was appointed as the first woman chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on **March 1, 2022**.
 
• She succeeded Ajay Tyagi, who completed his term as the SEBI chairman.
 
• Madhabi Puri Buch is a former executive director at ICICI Bank and has also served as a whole-time member of SEBI.
 
• Her leadership marked a historic milestone in the history of SEBI, reflecting the increasing representation of women in top regulatory positions.
 
• She is known for her technology-driven approach towards enhancing transparency and efficiency in the financial markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajay Tyagi:**

 
 
• Ajay Tyagi served as the chairman of SEBI from March 1, 2017, to February 28, 2022.
 
• He focused on reforms in the mutual fund industry and enhanced measures to protect investors.
 
• Under his tenure, SEBI implemented several regulations to strengthen corporate governance and improve market transparency.
 
 
 
• **UK Sinha:**
 
 
• UK Sinha was the SEBI chairman from February 2011 to March 2017.
 
• He played a key role in regulating alternative investment funds and tightening norms for insider trading.
 
• He introduced several measures to safeguard retail investors and boost market confidence.
 
 
 
• **CB Bhave:**
 
 
• CB Bhave served as the SEBI chairman from February 2008 to February 2011.
 
• During his tenure, SEBI introduced measures to improve transparency in IPO processes and strengthened regulations for credit rating agencies.
 
 
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI):**
 
 
• SEBI is the regulatory body for the securities and capital markets in India.
 
• It was established in 1988 and became a statutory body in 1992 under the SEBI Act.
 
• Its primary functions include protecting investor interests, regulating the securities market, and promoting the development of the market.
